instructions.title: How to use JWT Encoder/Decoder

steps.title: Choose a mode — Decode or Encode
steps.description: Use the Decode tab to inspect and verify an existing JWT, or switch to Encode to build and sign a new token from a header and payload. Mode switching is instant and local — nothing is sent to any server.

steps.title: Decode: paste your JWT token
steps.description: Copy your JWT from an API response, browser DevTools, or Authorization header and paste it into the input. The decoder instantly splits it into header, payload, and signature sections with a color-coded expiration countdown.

steps.title: Decode: verify the signature (optional)
steps.description: Expand the Verify Signature section, paste your secret (HMAC) or PEM public key (RSA/EC), and click Verify to cryptographically confirm the token is untampered — entirely in your browser via the Web Crypto API.

steps.title: Encode: pick an algorithm and write your claims
steps.description: Choose an algorithm (HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, or none), edit the payload JSON with your claims (sub, exp, iat, custom), and optionally add extra header fields like kid.

steps.title: Encode: provide the signing key and sign
steps.description: For HS* algorithms, enter a secret string. For RS*/ES* algorithms, paste your PKCS#8 PEM private key. Click Sign JWT to produce a signed token — the key stays in your browser at all times.

features: Both directions in one tool — decode existing tokens and encode new ones
Instant decoding into header, payload, and signature with a live color-coded expiration countdown
In-browser signing: HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, alg=none
In-browser verification: HS256, HS384, HS512, RS256, RS384, RS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, PS256
Zero data leakage — no token, secret, or key ever leaves your browser
Human-readable timestamps for exp, iat, nbf and all date claims
Header inspection — alg, kid, typ and any custom fields
Built on the native Web Crypto API — no external dependencies, works offline
useCases: Debug 401 Unauthorized errors by checking if the token has expired or contains wrong claims
Generate signed test tokens to exercise your API without running a full auth stack
Compare an expected payload with what your server actually emits
Inspect ID tokens from OAuth2/OIDC providers — Auth0, Okta, Cognito, Google, Firebase
Confirm the algorithm in the header matches what your server expects
Produce tokens with custom kid or claims for testing multi-tenant signing flows
Validate that sensitive data is not accidentally stored in the JWT payload
Share decoded token content with teammates for debugging without exposing secret keys
proTips: Copy tokens directly from browser DevTools — Network tab, Authorization header
Use alg=none only for local testing — any real service must reject unsigned tokens
For RS*/ES* signing use your private key; for verification paste only the public key — never share private keys with any online tool
The kid (key ID) field in the header tells you which key from your JWKS endpoint signed the token
After signing, click Decode ↗ on the output to round-trip the token and visually confirm the claims
Test with a deliberately invalid secret first to confirm the verifier correctly rejects it
Monitor the live countdown during load tests to catch short-lived tokens expiring mid-run
troubleshooting: Invalid JWT format — the token must have exactly three dot-separated parts: header.payload.signature
Signing error 'requires a secret' — HMAC algorithms need a non-empty secret string in the Secret Key field
Signing error 'requires a private key (PEM)' — RSA/EC algorithms need a PKCS#8 PEM private key including BEGIN/END lines
Signature shows INVALID for HS256 — check the secret is the raw string, not base64-encoded
RS256/ES256 verify fails — ensure the public key is in PEM format and includes the BEGIN/END header lines
Invalid payload JSON when encoding — the payload editor requires valid JSON; check for trailing commas or unquoted keys
Claims show unexpected values — the payload is base64url-encoded, not encrypted; anyone with the token can decode it
Signing and verification use the Web Crypto API, available in all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)

tagline: Decode, verify, encode and sign JWT tokens entirely in your browser
pageDescription: Free JWT encoder and decoder that handles both directions entirely in your browser — no server, no signup, nothing uploaded. Decode and inspect any JWT with a live expiration countdown, security analysis, and claims breakdown. Encode and sign new tokens with HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512 or alg=none for local testing. Verify signatures via the Web Crypto API without ever exposing secrets or private keys. Perfect for debugging authentication issues, generating test tokens for APIs, and validating JWT workflows with full privacy.
